Academic life · research · supervision

Twenty-five years at UTM, seen from the classroom and the server room.

I’ve spent most of my working life at the Faculty of Computing, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia — lecturer from 2006, Associate Professor since 2019, with a spell running the university’s IT services in between.

Biography · scroll trajectory

An academic life,
connected over time.

Scroll through the milestones that connect research, university service and postgraduate leadership.

01 / 2006
Lecturer at UTM

The beginning of a long academic chapter at the Faculty of Computing.

02 / 2007
Doctoral research

PhD at Heriot-Watt University, connecting bio-inspired search with articulated robot motion planning.

03 / 2012
Visiting researcher

A research chapter at Eindhoven University of Technology through Erasmus Mundus IDEAS.

04 / 2019—present
Associate Professor

Research, supervision and academic leadership converge at the Faculty of Computing.

01 — The long view
02 — Doctoral research
Heriot-Watt University, 2007

Foraging Ant Motion Planning for Articulated Robots

My PhD looked at how the search behaviour of foraging ants can be turned into a motion-planning strategy for articulated robots. In 2012 I spent a few months at Eindhoven University of Technology as a visiting researcher, on an Erasmus Mundus IDEAS scholarship.

PhD, Heriot-Watt University2007
Visiting Researcher, TU Eindhoven2012
Associate Professor, Faculty of Computing2019–present
Coordinator, PhD in Computer ScienceCurrent
03 — Current research

My research sits across pervasive computing, motion planning, and underwater wireless sensor networks, with an emphasis on work that has direct human use.

Computing in physical places

I’m also attached to KALAM, UTM’s centre for the study of the built environment in the Malay world, which has nothing to do with computing on paper and everything to do with it in practice. Positioning research needs a real, awkward, physical space to fail in before it works anywhere.

Research areas and interests →

04 — Supervision

Twenty-one PhD students and sixteen Master’s students have finished under my supervision.

I still post on Facebook when one of them passes their viva. It’s a small habit. It’s also the part of the job I’d keep even if everything else went away.
